If the model above represents $4$ wholes, use the model to solve the following division problem. Express your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.

$4÷\frac{3}{4}=$
{{field-1}}

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/60034ce6b9e7e7e5cd24c8f6f2f3d80a1bbc5d3a8532f3c4ccaeb3d89eaaeb1d.png)

 

Use the model above to calculate the value of $2 \div \dfrac{3}{7}.$
current_example.worked_solution:
To calculate ${\color{red}2} \div \dfrac{\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{3}}{\color{blue}7}$, we first need to divide each of the $\color{red}2$ wholes into $\color{blue}7$ equal parts.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/a373e9e5c6a5dc23240029d2d89fef66f4b9959ffef349f5ea351fffc897d3c8.png)

 

Next, we break this into groups of $\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{3}$:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/1cfe8f5a08ee9464489cacef94b0d94982def065a9ab290acc9ebbec6efc7bf7.png)

 

Note the following: 

- We got $\fbox{4}$ full groups.

- There are $\bbox[2pt, Moccasin]{2}$ pieces left over out of a possible group of $\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{3}.$ So the fractional part of our answer is 

$$
\dfrac{\bbox[2pt, Moccasin]{2}}{\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{3}}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
2 \div \dfrac{3}{7} = \fbox{4} \, \dfrac{\bbox[2pt, Moccasin]{2}}{\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{3}}.
$$
